bib.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness

read.skipped: Appendix B.3-C proofs and Tables 10-20 skimmed only (proof algebra and per-config timing grids)

question: Can exact attention be made faster and more memory-efficient on GPUs by accounting for reads and writes between HBM and on-chip SRAM?
hypothesis: Attention runtime is dominated by HBM accesses rather than FLOPs, so an IO-aware tiled algorithm with recomputation will be faster even with more FLOPs.
contributions: FlashAttention: IO-aware exact attention using tiling and recomputation in one fused CUDA kernel, with O(N) extra memory
IO complexity analysis: Theta(N^2 d^2 M^-1) HBM accesses vs Theta(Nd+N^2) standard, plus a lower bound
Block-sparse FlashAttention with IO complexity improved by the sparsity fraction
Faster training (BERT, GPT-2, LRA), longer context quality gains, first better-than-chance Path-X and Path-256

method.summary: A single fused CUDA kernel computes softmax(QK^T)V block by block in SRAM with running max and normaliser statistics, never writing the N x N matrix to HBM; the backward pass recomputes S and P from stored O and (m, l). Block-sparse variant skips zero blocks of a butterfly mask.
method.task: Attention kernel; end-to-end training of BERT-large, GPT-2, LRA models, long-document classification

limits: Needs a new hand-written CUDA kernel per attention variant, not transferable across GPU architectures
Speedup smaller on T4 (smaller SRAM) and with head dim 128 than on A100 head dim 64
Optimal only up to constants on a single GPU; multi-GPU IO analysis left open
Exact attention is slower than some approximate methods (e.g. Linformer) beyond 1K sequence length
FlashAttention backward is slightly slower than Apex FMHA at short lengths because of recomputation
Numerical equivalence argued by matching GPT-2 validation curves, no isolated numerical error analysis
Baselines Block Sparse, Longformer and BigBird measured without masking due to external bugs
